hosting.//rewrites: No catch-all to /404.html. A Hosting rewrite preserves the URL and returns 200, so every nonexistent path would serve the 404 page as a success and get indexed as duplicate content. With no rewrite, Hosting serves out/404.html with a real 404 status — which is what src/app/not-found.tsx emits it for.
hosting.//redirects: Every URL the Wix site published, taken from its sitemap while it was still up — after the cutover that list is unrecoverable. 301 rather than 302: these moves are permanent, and a 302 tells search engines to keep indexing the old URL. The source paths are Wix template names nobody chose, which is the whole reason for this table: /projects-7-2 is the ministry that feeds the homeless, and no one could read, guess, or say that out loud. Titles lie, so each destination was checked by loading the page: /team-3 is titled 'Calendar & Events' and is the activities page, NOT the clergy page it sounds like — the clergy bios are on /who-we-are. Mapping notes: /lesson-* are catechism pages (Intro, Young Christ, Saint Mina) but all three are empty Wix templates with no content; they land on /welcome because that is where a newcomer following an old link should end up, not because there is anything to preserve. Wix filed ministries and past events alike under `projects` — /projects-7-1, -7-2, -7-3 are the ongoing College & Young Professionals, Mother of Mercy, and St. Simon for Seniors ministries and now land on their own named anchors under /ministries; /projects-7, -7-4, -8 are the 2024 and 2023 festivals and Summer Camp 2024, which have already happened, so the calendar is the honest destination rather than a page invented for them. /portfolio already 404s on Wix and is redirected anyway, because it costs one line.
hosting.//headers: Cache headers for /service-worker.js and /manifest.webmanifest were removed: neither file exists yet, and there is no apps/website/public/ at all. Restore them in the same commit that adds the real PWA files.

functions.//predeploy: Rebuilds @spsm/shared and then the bundle. Without this a deploy can ship a lib/ built against an older shared package, which typechecks locally and fails at runtime in a way nothing catches.
functions.//ignore: .secret.local holds dummy values for the emulator and has no business in a deployed artifact. dist/ is the intermediate tsc output; only the bundled lib/ is needed.
